source_text: 18.63 καὶ ὁ σωτὴρ δὲ παρ' Ἰωάννῃ μόνου μνημονεύει τοῦ θεϊκοῦ πνεύματος λέγων· «ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ ἐκεῖνος, τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας, ὁδηγήσει ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν ἀλήθειαν πᾶσαν». 18.64 καὶ αἱ πράξεις ὡσαύτως περὶ τούτου πιστοῦνται· «τοῦ δὲ Πέτρου διανοουμένου περὶ τοῦ ῥήματος εἶπεν αὐτῷ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον· ἀναστὰς κατάβηθι καὶ πορεύου σὺν αὐτοῖς μηδὲν διακρινόμενος, διότι ἐγὼ ἀπέσταλκα αὐτούς», καὶ πάλιν· «τάδε λέγει τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον· ἀφορίσατέ μοι τὸν Παῦλον καὶ τὸν Βαρνά βαν εἰς τὸ ἔργον, ὁ προσκέκλημαι αὐτούς». καὶ πάλιν Πέτρῳ εἶπεν τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα· «ἀναστὰς πορεύθητι» εἰς τὸν οἶκον Κορνηλίου. 18.65 καὶ αὖθις κομψευόμεναι αἱ ἀποστολικαὶ πράξεις διατριβὴν παρέχουσιν τῷ τοιῷδε λόγῳ· περιέχουσιν γάρ· «τότε ὁ Παῦλος πλησθεὶς πνεύματος ἁγίου εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν», καὶ ἔτι· «ὁ γὰρ Πέτρος πλησθεὶς πνεύματος ἁγίου εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν λαόν». 18.66 Σημαίνεται δὲ ὁμοίως τὸ ἰσόρροπον καὶ ἰσοδύναμον τῶν παντίμων ὑποστάσεων καὶ ἐν τῷ τὸν δεσπότην θεὸν λόγον διὰ τῆς προλεχθείσης αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ βάπτισμα πανυμνήτου φωνῆς τὴν ἰσοτιμίαν ἑαυτῷ καὶ τῷ ἁγίῳ πνεύματι τὴν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα φυλάξαι· 18.67 δι' ἣν αἱ ἱεραὶ βίβλοι ποτὲ μὲν πρώτου μέμνηνται τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ οὕτω τοῦ υἱοῦ ἢ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος, ποτὲ δὲ πρώτου ἐπιμέμνηνται τοῦ υἱοῦ διὰ τὸ τῆς φύσεως ἀμέριστον καὶ τῆς θεολογίας τὸ ἀδιάφορον, 18.68 ὡς ὅταν λέγῃ Ἰὼβ τρανῶς τὴν τριάδα δηλῶν· 18.68 «ζῇ κύριος, ὃς οὕτω με κέκρικεν, καὶ ὁ παντοκράτωρ ὁ πικράνας μου τὴν ψυχήν· ἦ μὴν ἔτι τῆς πνοῆς μου ἐνούσης, πνεῦμα δὲ θεῖον τὸ περιόν μοι ἐν ῥισίν». τὸ ζωοποιοῦν με ἅγιον πνεῦμά φησιν καὶ ἀναπνέειν ἔτι ποιοῦν. 18.69 καὶ ὡς ἡνίκα Παῦλος Θεσσαλονικεῦσι τὸ δεύτερον γράφει· «αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς καὶ ὁ θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ παρακαλέσει ὑμῶν τὰς καρδίας», καὶ Γαλάταις· «Παῦλος ἀπόστολος οὐκ ἀπ' ἀνθρώπου οὐδὲ δι' ἀνθρώπου, ἀλλὰ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ θεοῦ πατρός», καὶ Κορινθίοις, ὡς προείρηται· «ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς καὶ ἡ κοινωνία τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος». 18.70 καὶ ὁ σωτὴρ δέ φησιν· «ἐλευσόμεθα ἐγὼ καὶ ὁ πατὴρ καὶ μονὴν παρ' αὐτῷ 21 ποιήσομεν». 18.71 Ποτὲ δὲ πρῶτον τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα ὀνομάζουσιν, μετέπειτα δὲ τὸν πατέρα ἢ τὸν υἱόν, ὡς ὅταν ∆αυῒδ ψάλλῃ· «ποῦ πορευθῶ ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματός σου, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ προσώπου σου ποῦ φύγω;» 18.72 καὶ ὁ Ἰὼβ τὸ εὔγνωμον δεικνὺς φάσκει· «πνεῦμα θεῖον τὸ ποιῆσάν με, πνοὴ δὲ παντοκράτορος ἡ διδάσκουσά με». 18.73 καὶ ὣς Παῦλος ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ ἐπιστολῇ Κορινθίοις γράφει· «διαιρέσεις δὲ χαρισμάτων εἰσίν, τὸ δὲ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα· καὶ διαιρέσεις διακονι ῶν εἰσιν, ὁ δὲ αὐτὸς κύριος· καὶ διαιρέσεις ἐνεργημάτων εἰσίν, ὁ δὲ αὐτὸς θεὸς ὁ ἐνεργῶν τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσιν». 18.74 Ποτὲ δὲ περὶ δύο ὑποστάσεων διαλέγονται ὁμωνύμως, ὡς ὅτε Ζαχαρίας λέγει· «εἶπεν κύριος πρὸς τὸν διάβολον· ἐπιτιμήσει κύριος ἐν σοί, διάβολε». 18.75 Καὶ ἀνωτέρω ἐδείχθη διὰ πλειόνων. 19.ν Περὶ τοῦ τὸ νῦν λεχθὲν περὶ τοῦ πατρός, ἄλλοτε περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ εἰρῆσθαι ἢ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος διὰ τὸ ἐν μιᾷ θεότητι τὴν τριάδα ὑπάρχειν. 19.1 Ἐν μιᾷ τοιγαροῦν θεότητι οἱ ἱεροφάνται τὴν ἔνδοξον τριάδα ἐπιστάμενοι καὶ τὴν θεολογίαν αὐτῆς ἐπίκοινον οὖσαν, ὅπερ νῦν εἰρήκασι περὶ τοῦ πατρός, ἄλλοτε ἄλλοι περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ ἢ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος διαγορεύουσιν, οὐκ ἐναντιούμενοι ἑαυτοῖς, ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸ καὶ ἡμᾶς εἰδέναι τοῦτό τε αὐτὸ τῆς ὀρθῆς πίστεως τὸ καίριον· καὶ ὡς, οἵας δ' ἂν ὑποστάσεως ἐπιμνησθῶμεν ἐκ παντός, καὶ τὴν ἄλλην τῇ πίστει συνανελάβομεν, ἅτε ἀχώριστον. 19.2 ἀψευδεῖν δὲ ἀνάγκη τοὺς ἀψευδεῖς ὑποφήτας θεοῦ καὶ δόξης ἀρνουμένης τὴν ἀλήθειαν καθαροὺς τοὺς τὴν ἁπλῆν καὶ ὄντως ἀλήθειαν, τουτέστιν τὴν ἀγαθότητα, τοῦ θεοῦ διδάσκοντας. 19.3 μὴ καθαροῖς γὰρ καθαρῶν ἐφάπτεσθαι μὴ οὐχὶ θεμιτόν φασιν· οἱ δὲ ἦσαν καθαροὶ καὶ πάσης ψευδοδοξίας ἀλλότριοι. 19.4 Εὑρήσομεν δὲ τοῦτο εὐθὺς εἰς τὴν θεοπτίαν, ἣν ἐθεάσατο Ἠσαΐας. τί δὲ μὴ πρῶτον ὅλου ἐκείνου ὡς ἔχει μνημονεύσω τοῦ χωρίου; 19.5 λέγει οὖν· «εἶδον τὸν κύριον Σαβαὼθ καθήμενον ἐπὶ θρόνου ὑψηλοῦ καὶ ἐπηρμένου, καὶ πλήρης ὁ οἶκος τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ. καὶ σεραφὶμ εἱστήκει σαν κύκλῳ αὐτοῦ· ἓξ πτέρυγες τῷ ἑνὶ καὶ ἓξ πτέρυγες τῷ ἑνί· καὶ ταῖς μὲν δυσὶ πτέρυξι κατεκάλυπτον τὰ πρόσωπα, ταῖς δὲ δυσὶ τοὺς πόδας, ταῖς δὲ δυσὶν ἐπέταντο· καὶ ἔκραζον ἕτερος πρὸς τὸν ἕτερον· ἅγιος ἅγιος
pass_a_gloss: 18.63 And the Saviour too, in John, mentions the divine Spirit alone, saying: 'but whenever that one comes, the Spirit of truth, he will guide you into all the truth'. 18.64 And the Acts likewise confirm [it] about this: 'and while Peter was pondering about the word, the Holy Spirit said to him: having risen, go down and journey with them, doubting nothing, because I have sent them', and again: 'these things says the Holy Spirit: set apart for me Paul and Barnabas for the work to which I have called them'. And again the Holy Spirit said to Peter: 'having risen, go', to the house of Cornelius. 18.65 And again the apostolic Acts, speaking elegantly, furnish occasion for lingering on such a statement; for they contain: 'then Paul, filled with Holy Spirit, said to him', and further: 'for Peter, filled with Holy Spirit, said to the people'. 18.66 And likewise the equal weight and equal power of the all-honoured hypostases is signified also in the Master, God the Word, having kept, through his all-hymned saying about baptism spoken before, the equality of honour toward the Father for himself and for the Holy Spirit; 18.67 on account of which the sacred books sometimes make mention first of the Father and so of the Son or of the Holy Spirit, and sometimes mention first the Son, on account of the undividedness of the nature and the non-difference of the speaking-of-God, 18.68 as when Job, clearly making plain the Trinity, says: 18.68 [number printed twice] 'the Lord lives, who has thus judged me, and the Almighty who embittered my soul; truly, while my breath is still in [me], and the divine Spirit which remains to me in [my] nostrils'. He says the Holy Spirit that makes me alive and makes [me] still breathe. 18.69 And as when Paul writes to Thessalonians the second time: 'and our Lord Jesus Christ himself and God and Father will comfort your hearts', and to Galatians: 'Paul an apostle not from man nor through man, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father', and to Corinthians, as has been said before: 'the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ and the love of God and Father and the communion of the Holy Spirit'. 18.70 And the Saviour too says: 'we will come, I and the Father, and we will make a dwelling with him'. 18.71 And sometimes they name the Holy Spirit first, and afterwards the Father or the Son, as when David sings: 'where shall I go from your Spirit, and from your face where shall I flee?' 18.72 And Job, showing his grateful mind, says: 'a divine Spirit [is] the one that made me, and the breath of the Almighty the one teaching me'. 18.73 And thus Paul writes in the first letter to Corinthians: 'and there are distributions of gifts, but the same Spirit; and there are distributions of ministries, but the same Lord; and there are distributions of workings, but the same God who works all things in all'. 18.74 And sometimes they discourse about two hypostases with the same name, as when Zechariah says: 'the Lord said to the devil: the Lord will rebuke in you, devil'. 18.75 And above it was shown through more [instances]. 19.ν [Chapter title:] About the thing now said about the Father having been said at another time about the Son or the Holy Spirit, on account of the Trinity existing in one Godhead. 19.1 So then the revealers of sacred things, knowing the glorious Trinity in one Godhead and its speaking-of-God being common, what they have now said about the Father, at other times others declare about the Son or the Holy Spirit, not opposing themselves, but on account of our knowing too both this very thing, the crucial point of the right faith, and that, whatever hypostasis we mention, by all means we have also taken up together the other in faith, as inseparable. 19.2 And it is necessary that the unlying interpreters of God be unlying, and that those who teach the simple and really-being truth, that is the goodness, of God be pure of opinion denying the truth. 19.3 For they say it is not lawful for the not-pure to lay hold of the pure; and these were pure and strangers to all false belief. 19.4 And we shall find this straightaway in the vision of God which Isaiah beheld. And why shall I not first recall that whole place as it stands? 19.5 He says then: 'I saw the Lord Sabaoth seated on a throne high and lifted up, and the house full of his glory. And seraphim stood around him; six wings to the one and six wings to the one; and with the two wings they covered the faces, and with the two the feet, and with the two they flew; and they cried, the one to the other: holy, holy [...]
pass_b_english: And in John the Saviour too mentions the divine Spirit alone, saying, “But when he comes, the Spirit of truth, he will guide you into all the truth” (John 16:13). The Acts likewise confirm this: “While Peter was pondering the word, the Holy Spirit said to him, ‘Rise, go down, and go with them without any hesitation, for I have sent them’” (Acts 10:19-20). And again: “Thus says the Holy Spirit: ‘Set apart for me Paul and Barnabas for the work to which I have called them’” (Acts 13:2). And again the Holy Spirit said to Peter, “Rise and go,” to the house of Cornelius.

And once more the apostolic Acts, with a certain elegance, give room to dwell on a statement of this kind. They contain: “Then Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to him” (Acts 13:9-10), and further: “For Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to the people” (Acts 4:8).

In the same way, the equal weight and equal power of the all-honoured hypostases is signified in this too: that the Master, God the Word, by his all-praised saying about baptism, which I mentioned before (Matthew 28:19), kept for himself and for the Holy Spirit their equality of honour with the Father. Because of it the sacred books sometimes mention the Father first and then the Son or the Holy Spirit, and sometimes mention the Son first, since the nature is undivided and there is no difference in the way the three are spoken of as God.

So Job, plainly showing the Trinity, says: “As the Lord lives, who has judged me thus, and the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter: truly, while my breath is still in me, and the divine Spirit that remains to me in my nostrils” (Job 27:2-3). He means the Holy Spirit, who gives him life and still makes him breathe.

So too when Paul writes to the Thessalonians the second time: “Now our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God and Father, will comfort your hearts” (2 Thessalonians 2:16-17); and to the Galatians: “Paul, an apostle, not from man nor through man, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father” (Galatians 1:1); and to the Corinthians, as was said before: “The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ and the love of God and Father and the communion of the Holy Spirit” (2 Corinthians 13:14). And the Saviour says, “I and the Father will come, and we will make our dwelling with him” (John 14:23).

Sometimes they name the Holy Spirit first, and afterwards the Father or the Son, as when David sings, “Where shall I go from your Spirit, and from your face where shall I flee?” (Psalm 139:7). And Job, showing his grateful mind, says, “It is the divine Spirit that made me, and the breath of the Almighty that teaches me” (Job 33:4). And so Paul writes in the first letter to the Corinthians: “There are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit; and there are varieties of ministries, but the same Lord; and there are varieties of workings, but the same God who works all things in all” (1 Corinthians 12:4-6).

Sometimes they speak of two hypostases by the same name, as when Zechariah says, “The Lord said to the devil, ‘The Lord will rebuke you, devil’” (Zechariah 3:2). This was also shown above at greater length.
That what is said at one time of the Father is said at another of the Son or of the Holy Spirit, because the Trinity exists in one Godhead.

The revealers of holy things, then, knowing the glorious Trinity in one Godhead, and that what is said of it as God is shared in common, set forth at other times, some of them, about the Son or the Holy Spirit what others have just said about the Father. They do not contradict themselves. They do it so that we too may know this very point, the crucial thing in right faith: that whichever hypostasis we mention, we have by all means taken up the other with it in faith, since it cannot be separated.

The truthful interpreters of God must speak truly; and those who teach the simple and real truth of God, that is, his goodness, must be clean of every opinion that denies the truth. For they say it is not lawful for the impure to touch the pure; and these men were pure, and strangers to all false belief.

We shall find this at once in the vision of God that Isaiah saw. But why should I not first recall that whole passage as it stands? He says, then (Isaiah 6:1-3): “I saw the Lord Sabaoth sitting on a throne high and lifted up, and the house was full of his glory. And seraphim stood around him; six wings to the one and six wings to the other; with two wings they covered their faces, with two their feet, and with two they flew. And they cried one to the other, ‘Holy, holy …

lemmas.gloss: speaking of someone as God, divine title

choices.issue: Old draft garbled, wrong references, fillers
choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. Wrong references fixed: '(1 Thess 3:11)' for Didymus' 'to the Thessalonians the second time', which is 2 Thessalonians 2:16-17 (reader report, 1-thessalonians/SOURCE_ISSUES.md); '(2 Cor 13:13)' (Greek verse number) made 2 Corinthians 13:14; '(Acts 10:20)' removed from the third Acts saying, which is not worded so in Acts (now a possible allusion, Acts 11:12); Acts 10:19 widened to 10:19-20 and Acts 13:9 to 13:9-10; Matthew 28:19 added; all names written in full. Clauses fixed: 18.63 μόνου goes with the Spirit ('the Savior alone mentions' was wrong); 18.64-18.65 αἱ πράξεις is the book of Acts, not 'the deeds', and κομψευόμεναι … διατριβὴν παρέχουσιν is not 'being elegant, provide a demonstration'; 18.66 was unreadable; 18.68 τὸ περιόν is 'that remains', not 'surrounds', and the gloss on the Spirit who gives life had fillers [that He is], [it]; 18.70 μονήν is 'dwelling' ('with Him alone' was wrong); 18.71 ποτέ ('sometimes') was dropped; 18.72 τὸ εὔγνωμον is a grateful mind, not 'good conscience'; 18.75 'shown more clearly through many [examples]'; the 19.ν chapter title ran into the text; 19.1-19.2 were garbled ('the truthful ones, who deny the truth of glory'); 19.3 ψευδοδοξία is false belief, not 'false glory'. Bracket fillers [the relation], [that He is], [it], [examples], [mention] removed.

choices.term: παρ' Ἰωάννῃ μόνου μνημονεύει τοῦ θεϊκοῦ πνεύματος
choices.english: in John the Saviour too mentions the divine Spirit alone
choices.why: μόνου agrees with πνεύματος: this belongs to the list of texts that name the Spirit alone (18.60-18.65).
Didymus' text has ῥήματος where Acts 10:19 has ὁράματος ('the vision'); his wording is kept.

choices.term: κομψευόμεναι αἱ ἀποστολικαὶ πράξεις διατριβὴν παρέχουσιν τῷ τοιῷδε λόγῳ
choices.english: the apostolic Acts, with a certain elegance, give room to dwell on a statement of this kind
choices.why: Didymus notes that Acts again names the Spirit alone ('filled with the Holy Spirit'), giving matter for reflection.

choices.term: διὰ τῆς προλεχθείσης αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ βάπτισμα πανυμνήτου φωνῆς
choices.english: by his all-praised saying about baptism, which I mentioned before (Matthew 28:19)
choices.why: The baptismal command named in 18.35; a clear allusion, so it is cited.

choices.term: τῆς θεολογίας τὸ ἀδιάφορον; τὴν θεολογίαν αὐτῆς ἐπίκοινον
choices.english: there is no difference in the way the three are spoken of as God; what is said of it as God is shared in common
choices.why: θεολογία in Didymus is the naming of a Person as God, not academic theology.
The copy-text prints the number 18.68 twice; numbers are not printed in the reading text.

choices.term: πνεῦμα δὲ θεῖον τὸ περιόν μοι ἐν ῥισίν … τὸ ζωοποιοῦν με ἅγιον πνεῦμά φησιν
choices.english: the divine Spirit that remains to me in my nostrils … He means the Holy Spirit, who gives him life and still makes him breathe
choices.why: Didymus explains Job's words in Job's voice ('me'); English reports it in the third person so the gloss is not mistaken for Scripture.

choices.english: to the Thessalonians the second time … will comfort your hearts
choices.why: 2 Thessalonians 2:16-17; Didymus' text has the future παρακαλέσει where the letter has a wish, and his wording is kept.
Didymus' text has the future; 'the Lord' who speaks and 'the Lord' who rebukes are his two hypostases named alike.

choices.english: That what is said at one time of the Father is said at another of the Son or of the Holy Spirit, because the Trinity exists in one Godhead.
choices.why: Chapter title in the copy-text; set as its own short paragraph.
Didymus' word for the inspired writers; literally 'those who show sacred things'. Kept as a description rather than 'hierophants'.

choices.term: μὴ καθαροῖς γὰρ καθαρῶν ἐφάπτεσθαι μὴ οὐχὶ θεμιτόν φασιν
choices.english: For they say it is not lawful for the impure to touch the pure
choices.why: A proverb from Plato (Phaedo 67b), introduced with 'they say'; not Scripture, so no reference.

choices.term: ἀνέτειλεν … καὶ ἔκραζον ἕτερος πρὸς τὸν ἕτερον· ἅγιος ἅγιος
choices.why: The section ends inside the quotation; the reference is placed before it because the quotation does not close here. Ends with '…'.

choices.term: Βαρνά βαν; διακονι ῶν; εἱστήκει σαν; αὐτῷ 21 ποιήσομεν
choices.why: Words split by line breaks are read as single words; the printed number 21 inside 18.70 is page debris and is skipped.
